name: Lê Hồng Quang
title: Software Engineer
summary:
• Experience: 10+ years in frontend (6 in ReactJS, 2 in AngularJS, 2 in VueJS). 4 years fullstack (NodeJS, Python, SQL, REST, GraphQL). 2 years in DevOps (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), and 2 years building AI agents (automated workflows, Agent Skills, token optimization, doc-driven development, MCP servers — with code review, security checks, monitoring, and error tracing in the loop).

• Architecting: I lead design with the C4 model and RFC/ADRs, and I take every proposal through performance, scalability, security, operations, and cost. A business goal becomes clear requirements, then a design the team can build. I stay with it from POC through production and monitoring.

• Stakeholder Management: I work most closely with the Architecture Review group, Product Owners, Engineering Managers, Security/SRE, and peer leads. When I need a yes from leadership, I bring 2–3 options, a trade-off matrix (cost, risk, time-to-market, maintainability), POC evidence, success metrics, and a rollout/rollback plan.

• Engineering Leadership: 2 years leading a team of 3 — frontend standards, code review, tech-debt work, and mentoring.

workExperience.description:
WebAI Workflow Agent — An LLM workflow that runs daily UI tasks in the background. Input is a Slack message or a JIRA ticket; output is a merge request with analytics, a preview URL, and a feedback loop.

• Role: Fullstack (I proposed it and built the POC), Team Lead of a team of 3 for 2 years

• Tech Doc: https://shorturl.quang.work/ydXJam

• Impact:

• Built an always-on AI workflow that automates UI tasks and opens MRs with the Claude Code SDK and GitLab CI/CD as the sandbox. 40+ web apps at Grab use it, and it is still growing.

• Shipped a Slack-first self-service onboarding UI with multi-repo routing, so teams no longer set it up by hand.

• Built a FastAPI backend with REST APIs for the Slack bot, HashiCorp Vault for secrets, and Datadog, Kibana, and Grafana for production monitoring.

• Designed it with C4 and an RFC: queue-based concurrency, stateless workers on CI runners, Vault secrets with least-privilege tokens, sandboxed runs, Datadog alerts plus an on-call runbook, and an LLM token budget per task.

• Walked Architecture Review, Product, Engineering Managers, and Security through a build-vs-buy trade-off matrix, POC benchmarks, and the hours we expected to save — and got leadership approval.

Global Build Tool — An NPM CLI for Webpack and Rspack that simplifies frontend builds across Grab.

• Role: Fullstack

• Tech Doc: https://shorturl.quang.work/7lcVYT

• Impact:

• Built the CLI on Webpack and Rspack to untangle legacy builds, cutting build time by 50%.

• Rolled it out as the shared build setup for 120+ web apps at Grab.

• Added Micro Frontend support (Module Federation) in NodeJS/TypeScript, so apps can ship in smaller pieces.

• Won over Engineering Managers and app owners with a cost/benefit trade-off (build speed, maintenance, migration risk, CI cost), then rolled it out in phases with a rollback path. It is now Grab's standard build tool.

Coban UI — A portal for data-streaming infrastructure and pipelines (Kafka, Flink).

• Role: Maintainer

• Impact:

• Shipped the Kafka/Flink portal with Product Owners, Engineering Managers, and data platform teams across regions, so the team could hit its OKRs.

• Designed the UI with Ant Design, Framer Motion for animation, and React Flow for the charts, so a pipeline is something you can actually read.

• Hooked up Datadog RUM for live metrics and logs, so the system stays visible around the clock.

• Set it up as a Micro Frontend with React, Redux, and Jest.

WebKit monorepo — A monorepo that scaffolds frontend projects at Grab.

• Role: Maintainer | On-call Duty

• Impact:

• Gave Grab's frontend a shared setup with Lerna/Nx and scaffolding templates, so a new project starts faster.

• Wrote reusable GitLab CI/CD pipelines so teams stop hand-tuning deploys.

• As a core maintainer, I review MRs and cover on-call for the apps on this repo.

React Structured Search — An NPM library for autocomplete search with live suggestions.

• Role: Fullstack

• Demo: https://quang.work/projects/react-structured-search

• Impact:

• Built a React/TypeScript library for GitHub-style structured search, with autocomplete and richer queries.

• Used it to add global search across several portals, one interface for finding different kinds of resources.

• Documented the components in Storybook and bundled the package with Webpack, so other teams could pick it up.

Concedo Auth — An NPM library for Concedo OIDC, Grab's authentication standard.

• Role: Fullstack

• Impact:

• Built a ReactJS/TypeScript library so apps can plug into OAuth without each team reinventing the flow.

• Adopted by 60+ web apps, with one auth workflow and JWT for consistent security.

FoodMe — A site for booking restaurants and writing food reviews.

• Role: Team Lead of a team of 3 for 2 years

• Demo: https://quang.work/projects/foodme

• Impact:

• Led the frontend rewrite and code reviews, and mentored juniors on TypeScript and Redux Toolkit.

• Set up state with Redux Saga and Reselect, and gated commits with Husky and ESLint.

• Added Google Maps SDK for location, and AWS Cognito for auth and sessions.

GoFox — A blockchain NFT marketplace.

• Role: Fullstack

• Demo: https://quang.work/projects/gofox

• Impact:

• Built a MERN NFT marketplace on Ethereum, with decentralized auctions, lending, and trading.

• Connected multiple wallets and smart contracts with Ethers.js and Web3.js.

• Managed state with Redux Toolkit, and ran CI/CD on Azure and Google Cloud (GCP).

FunArcade — A Bitcoin gambling site.

• Role: Frontend

• Demo: https://quang.work/projects/funarcade

• Impact:

• Built a high-traffic Bitcoin gaming platform from scratch, with Socket.io for live updates and Redux Saga/Reselect for state.

• Brought in TypeScript, ESLint, and Husky pre-commit hooks.

• Shipped deploys with GitHub Actions onto Azure.

iVIVU Member — Authentication, authorization, and a points rewards system.

• Role: Fullstack

• Demo: https://quang.work/projects/ivivuMember

• Impact:

• Built the loyalty platform from scratch, taking it from Figma to production.

• Designed the SQL schema and REST API that sync points with the booking engine, secured with JWT and refresh tokens.

• Used SSR to help SEO and the first load.

iVIVU Experience — A site for reviewing food, hotels, and places to visit.

• Role: Fullstack

• Demo: https://quang.work/projects/ivivuExperience

• Impact:

• Built a travel guide from scratch with Angular SSR, from Figma to a fast, SEO-friendly UI.

• Added map search and reviews so people can explore a destination and come back to it.

iVIVU Flight — A Chrome extension that crawls flight prices.

• Role: Fullstack

• Impact:

• Built a JavaScript Chrome extension that pulls flight prices from several airlines.

• Added a live comparison view so the better fare is easy to spot.

Olay Skin Advisor — A feature on Olay.com.

• Role: Maintainer

• Demo: https://quang.work/projects/olay

• Impact:

• Turned designs from Figma, Sketch, and PSD into responsive UI for a global skincare site.

• Worked in a 15+ person Agile team, maintaining and tuning features on .NET MVC.

items.title: Frontend Architect with Fullstack Capability
items.description:
• Main stack is NextJS, ReactJS, and TypeScript. Comfortable with micro-frontends, design systems, OAuth, and JWT.

• On the backend side of fullstack work: PostgreSQL/MySQL, REST, GraphQL, NodeJS, and Python.

• Also SSR, ES6+, SEO, Socket.io, Webpack, Babel, NPM package versioning, and blockchain (Web3).

• I use AI agents in the daily workflow (Claude Code SDK, Cursor, Copilot, AGENTS.md) to move faster.

• UI kits I reach for: Ant Design, Material UI, Shadcn UI, Tailwind CSS.

• Debugging and performance profiling: Google Lighthouse, React DevTools, GTmetrix, WebPageTest.

items.title: Architecting & Stakeholder Management
items.description:
• How I design: C4 (Context, Container, Component, Code), RFC/ADR, plus sequence and data-flow diagrams, so a decision is easy to revisit.

• What I make explicit: performance, scalability, security, operations, and cost, including capacity assumptions and failure modes.

• Who I bring in: Architecture Review, Product Owner, Engineering Manager, Security/SRE, and peer leads — to stress-test a solution before we commit.
